vignette: Malua, a 51-year-old male from Oceania, works as a welder and is married to his longtime partner, Lina. Malua's life took a sudden and unexpected turn two years ago when he was involved in a life-threatening motor vehicle collision while driving home from work one evening. Since then, his days have been filled with an overwhelming sense of unease that lingers long after the incident. On the day of the accident, Malua had just finished another busy shift at the shipyard where he works as a welder. It was a typical afternoon; the sun was setting behind him as he drove home on the winding coastal road near his village. Suddenly, a car swerved into his lane without warning, causing a collision that left Malua's vehicle spinning off the side of the road and down an embankment. Miraculously, he survived with only minor injuries, but the memory of that moment continues to haunt him. Since the accident, Malua has experienced intense flashbacks whenever he hears loud noises or sees vehicles swerving on the road. The sound of sirens can trigger a panic attack, sending waves of nausea and sweating through his body as he relives the terrifying moments of the collision. He often finds himself checking his mirrors repeatedly while driving, convinced that another car might suddenly appear out of nowhere. At work, Malua's anxiety manifests in different ways. The rhythmic hum of welding equipment and the occasional clanging of metal can sometimes evoke memories of the crash, making it difficult for him to concentrate on his tasks. He has developed a heightened sense of alertness, constantly scanning his surroundings for any sign of danger. His hands tremble slightly when he picks up his welding torch, a physical manifestation of the internal chaos he experiences. Malua's relationships have also been affected by his PTSD symptoms. Lina notices that he often isolates himself and becomes irritable without warning. He has trouble falling asleep at night because of nightmares where he relives the crash in vivid detail. These sleepless nights leave him exhausted during the day, further exacerbating his irritability and frustration. Lina tries to support him as much as she can, but Malua often pushes her away when she reaches out to comfort him. He feels a deep sense of guilt for not being able to protect himself or Lina from what happened. The fear that he might get into another accident haunts him, making it difficult for him to engage in activities they once enjoyed together. Malua's work as a welder has also been impacted by his PTSD symptoms. He finds it challenging to maintain focus during long shifts and often feels overwhelmed by the sensory stimuli at the shipyard. His colleagues have noticed that he sometimes appears distracted or distant, which can be dangerous in an environment where precision and attention are crucial. Despite these challenges, Malua remains committed to his job and his family. Lina has encouraged him to seek help, but Malua struggles with opening up about his experiences. He fears being seen as weak and worries that others will judge him for not being able to move past the trauma on his own. However, he is starting to recognize how much his symptoms are affecting both his work and personal life. Malua continues to navigate this new reality, learning to manage his intense emotions and intrusive thoughts. He has started to take small steps towards healing, such as taking short breaks during the day to practice deep breathing exercises or going for walks along the beach near their home. These moments of peace provide temporary relief from the constant anxiety that surrounds him. As Malua continues on this journey, he holds onto hope that with time and effort, he can find a way to reclaim his life and rediscover the sense of normalcy he once knew before the accident.
